html:
The Battle of Austerlitz was fought on 2 December 1805 near Austerlitz, now Slavkov u Brna in the Czech Republic. Napoleon's army of about 70,000 beat a larger Russian and Austrian army. It is also called the Battle of the Three Emperors, because Tsar Alexander I and the Austrian emperor Francis were both present.

In 1805 Britain, Austria and Russia joined against France. Napoleon marched into Germany, captured an Austrian army at Ulm in October and took Vienna in November. Far from home, he needed a quick win, so he acted weak. He gave up the high ground of the Pratzen Heights and kept his right wing thin. The allies moved troops down from the heights to attack that wing. Then French infantry climbed out of the morning mist, took the heights and split the allied army. The allies lost at least a third of their army. The French lost about 9,000 men.

Austria made peace within weeks and gave up land in Italy and Germany. In 1806 the thousand-year-old Holy Roman Empire was dissolved, and Napoleon grouped the German states into his Confederation of the Rhine. Austerlitz is usually seen as his finest victory in the Napoleonic Wars.
